newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc ends lower on EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc ends lower on EMU stability pact.

text.p: 1545 GMT - The Swiss franc ended easier but off its lows against the dollar and mark, weighed down by the EU's stability pact for the euro currency and the Swiss National Bank's clear reiteration on Friday that it would keep monetary policy loose.
"The fact that the stability pact was agreed speaks against the franc, which won't profit as much as a safe haven currency," one dealer at a Swiss bank said.
* Dollar closes at 1.3279/3284 francs, up from 1.3118/3123 at Friday's close and 1.3235/3245 at the opening after hitting a high just below 1.33 francs
* Mark ends at 85.42/45 Swiss centimes, up from 85.06/09 at the close and the opening 85.18/20. It was at its highest levels since May 1995
* Swiss combined producer/import price index fell 2.5 percent year on year in November
The franc was at key technical points at 1.3280/90 to the dollar and 85.55 to the mark, but dealers said it still had room to drop on the SNB's generous line. -- Zurich +41 1 631 7340
